title: Present Continuous: Complete the Sentences
inst: Complete the sentences with the Present Continuous (+ or -).
theory:
Present Continuous: Affirmative and Negative

Structure: Subject + am / is / are + Verb with -ing

  • Affirmative (+): I am sleeping. / He / She / It is sleeping. / We / You / They are sleeping.
  • Negative (-): I'm not sleeping. / He / She / It isn't sleeping. / We / You / They aren't sleeping.

Spelling Rules for -ing

  • Most verbs: wear → wearing, help → helping
  • Verbs ending in -e: delete the -e: make → making, dance → dancing
  • One-syllable verbs with consonant-vowel-consonant: double the final letter: run → running, stop → stopping

items.q: 1. Ray ___ (wear) a warm jacket today.
2. Hop and Bee ___ (not wait) for the bus.
3. We ___ (prepare) our clothes for school.
4. Look! The boy ___ (run) in the race.
items.why: -ing spelling: double the final letter (run - running)

items.q: 5. I ___ (not sleep) right now because I am awake.
6. She ___ (make) a dress out of paper.
7. The students ___ (not pack) their bags yet.

title: Present Continuous: Correct the Mistake
inst: Find the mistake in each sentence and write the correct sentence.

items.q: 1. She wearing a blue hoodie today.
a: She is wearing a blue hoodie today.
She's wearing a blue hoodie today.
items.why: Present Continuous needs am / is / are before the -ing verb

items.q: 2. They isn't running together.
3. We are makeing clothes from plastic.
a: We are making clothes from plastic.

items.q: 4. I aren't doing my English homework.
a: I'm not doing my English homework.
I am not doing my English homework.
items.why: Negative with I: I'm not + verb-ing

title: Questions and Short Answers
inst: For each prompt, write a question. Then write the short answer to that question: Yes (✔) or No (✖).
theory:
Questions and Short Answers

Put Am / Is / Are before the person to make a question:

  • I: Am I running? → Yes, I am. / No, I'm not.
  • He / She / It: Is he / she / it running? → Yes, he is. / No, he isn't.
  • We / You / They: Are we / you / they running? → Yes, they are. / No, they aren't.

items.q: 1. Write the question: Sarah and Oliver / wear / jeans
a: Are Sarah and Oliver wearing jeans?
items.why: Questions: Am / Is / Are before the person

items.q: 2. Now write the short answer to question 1: Yes (✔)
items.why: Short answer with they: Yes, they are. / No, they aren't.

items.q: 3. Write the question: Dad / watch / TV
items.why: Questions: Am / Is / Are before the person

items.q: 4. Now write the short answer to question 3: Yes (✔)
items.why: Short answer with he: Yes, he is. / No, he isn't.

items.q: 5. Write the question: Sarah / read / a book
items.why: Questions: Am / Is / Are before the person

items.q: 6. Now write the short answer to question 5: No (✖)
items.why: Short answer with she: Yes, she is. / No, she isn't.

items.q: 7. Write the question: The cat / sleep / on the chair
a: Is the cat sleeping on the chair?
items.why: Questions: Am / Is / Are before the person

items.q: 8. Now write the short answer to question 7: Yes (✔)
items.why: Short answer with it: Yes, it is. / No, it isn't.

items.q: 9. Write the question: Mum and Sarah / wear / glasses
a: Are Mum and Sarah wearing glasses?
items.why: Questions: Am / Is / Are before the person

items.q: 10. Now write the short answer to question 9: No (✖)
items.why: Short answer with they: Yes, they are. / No, they aren't.

title: Why and Because: Match
inst: Match each question with its answer.
theory:
"Why...?" and "Because..."

  • Why asks for a reason (question).
  • Because gives the reason (answer).
  • Example: — Why are you running? / — Because I'm late for dinner!

items.q: 1. Why are you wearing pajamas?
o: A. Because it's my mum's birthday.
B. Because I am going to bed.
D. Because it is the weekend!
items.a: B. Because I am going to bed.
items.why: Why asks for a reason; Because gives the reason

items.q: 2. Why are you making a cake?

B. Because I am going to bed.
D. Because it is the weekend!
items.a: A. Because it's my mum's birthday.
items.why: Why asks for a reason; Because gives the reason

items.q: 3. Why aren't you studying?
o: A. Because it's my mum's birthday.
B. Because I am going to bed.
D. Because it is the weekend!

o: A. Because it's my mum's birthday.
B. Because I am going to bed.

title: Regular Verbs: Add -ed
inst: Complete the sentences with the past simple of the verb in brackets.
theory:
Past Simple: Regular Verbs

Structure: Subject + Verb + -ed

  • Most verbs: add -ed: play → played, watch → watched
  • Verbs ending in -e: add -d: dance → danced, like → liked
  • Consonant + y: change y to i + -ed: study → studied, carry → carried
  • One vowel + one consonant: double the final letter: stop → stopped, plan → planned

Time expressions: yesterday, last night, last week, two days ago, in 2020

items.q: 1. Yesterday I ___ (watch) a film.
2. She ___ (visit) her grandmother last weekend.
3. We ___ (dance) at the party on Saturday.
4. He ___ (study) for the test last night.
items.why: Consonant + y: change y to i + -ed

items.q: 5. They ___ (stop) at the shop two days ago.
items.why: One vowel + one consonant: double the final letter

items.q: 6. My mum ___ (cook) dinner yesterday.
7. The children ___ (play) in the park last Sunday.
8. I ___ (carry) my bag to school this morning.
items.why: Consonant + y: change y to i + -ed

title: Irregular Verbs
inst: Write the past simple of the irregular verb in brackets.
theory:
Past Simple: Irregular Verbs

Irregular verbs do not end in -ed. You have to learn them!

  • go → went, have → had, see → saw, eat → ate
  • buy → bought, make → made, take → took, give → gave
  • write → wrote, drink → drank, be → was / were

Past Simple: Affirmative and Negative

  • Affirmative (+): She visited her aunt. / He went home.
  • Negative (-): Subject + didn't + base form: She didn't visit her aunt. / He didn't go home.

Remember: after didn't the verb stays in the base form (didn't go, NOT didn't went).

  • Did you watch TV? → Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.
  • Did he play football? → Yes, he did. / No, he didn't.

title: Past of To Be: Was and Were
inst: Complete with was, were, wasn't or weren't.
theory:
Past Simple of To Be

  • I / He / She / It → was / wasn't
  • We / You / They → were / weren't
  • Questions: Was he at home? / Were you at the party?

We do not use did with the verb to be.
